newsitem.title: sri lanka: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - April 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - April 29.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Transport, Environment and Womens Affairs Minister Srimani Athulathmudali's portfolio may be changed during a planned cabinet reshuffle early next month, sources close to the government say.
Government hospitals disrupted after nurses struke work protesting non-implementation of proposed salary revision.
Police take into custody a Tamil woman serving as a broadcaster at a private television station on suspicion of harbouring plans to assassinate Deputy Defence Minister Anuruddha Ratwatte.

Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels destroy special "Tamil Eelam" notes printed in 1992 by them to be used as the legal currency in rebel-controlled areas in the north. The rebels were forced to abandon their northern Jaffna peninsula stronghold in April last year after security forces captured it after a long offensive.
Twenty two May Day rallies to be staged by political parties and recognised trade unions on May 1.
A proposal to increase electricity tariffs by 30 percent to be submitted to the cabinet by Power and Energy Minister Anuruddha Ratwatte on Wednesday.

Main opposition United National Party (UNP) appoints special committee to spearhead campaign to oppose a Broadcasting Authority Bill proposed by the government. UNP says the bill would unfairly influence private broadcasting networks.
